content:
In HBO's Sunday episode of Last Week Tonight, Oliver turned his sights on his incoming, MAGA-aligned new boss, sharply criticizing the role the player had in pushing Stephen Colbert off the television screen.

The dig was particularly clever because Oliver, while assuring Ellison that he would 'absolutely not make fun of' him, managed to land a jab — and he did so while in the middle of an entire segment examining UnitedHealthcare.

Oliver opened with a story as a setup for the joke: cancer patient Kate Weissman was denied coverage by UnitedHealthcare for a life-saving treatment, even though most of her doctors, affiliated with the Harvard system, supported the procedure. Weissman's parents ended up paying $95,000 out of pocket for the treatment.

Oliver said: 'Whether or not you have rich parents to fall back on should absolutely not be the system that determines whether you get medically necessary care.' At that moment, a photo of Ellison popped up beside the screen. He continued: 'Even if that does appear to be the system that put you in charge of HBO.'

Oliver said: 'Yes, the business daddy I'm about to acquire has a real business daddy behind him.' At that moment, Ellison's photo enlarged, with a photo of his father — billionaire Oracle CEO Larry Ellison — added beside it.

Paramount reached a deal on Monday that removed the 'last major obstacle' to its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, according to the New York Times. Warner Bros. Discovery is the parent company of HBO, the network on which Last Week Tonight airs.

HBO will be folded into Paramount's larger media empire, which already includes the CBS television network and is currently being overhauled under his leadership by David Ellison.

Oliver adjusted his tone with a hint of sarcasm that sounded almost sincere, saying: 'To be clear, I have a tremendous amount of respect for this.' Then he added: 'And I would absolutely never make fun of you for it, unlike that pesky Stephen Colbert.'
